Printed title / caption: Facility counts and travel times answer different questions, and the province needs both. A registration is not a building, a building within reach is not an open service, and an open service is not necessarily ready to treat the patient in front of it. Section 4.3 sets out a consistency test that qualifies how far that result can be carried.

Label: EXHIBIT 4
Printed title / caption: Tuberculosis notification against expected incidence, by municipality
Source note as printed: Note. Derived. Notified cases apply the municipal tuberculosis case notification rate (Department of Health, n.d.-a, 2022 indicator year) to the 2024 census population (Philippine Statistics Authority, 2025c); expected incident cases apply the WHO-estimated Philippine incidence of 625 per 100,000 (World Health Organization, 2025) to the same population. Provincial aggregate: approximately 1,285 notified against approximately 4,634 expected, a detection ratio of 27.7 per cent. Three cautions attach. A national incidence rate applied to a provincial population establishes order of magnitude only, and the WHO estimate carries a 95 per cent uncertainty interval of 344 to 1,020 per 100,000. A 2022 notification rate is applied to a 2024 population. And the municipal spread of 70.3 to 303.6 per 100,000 — a fourfold range, against the eighteenfold range recorded in Lanao del Sur — is narrow enough that it measures case-finding effort rather than disease distribution. The City of Cotabato, not shown, notifies at 714.6 per 100,000, more than twice the highest municipal rate; that is an attribution artefact of city facilities notifying cases resident elsewhere and is a reason not to fold the city into provincial tuberculosis planning.
